description: Stereo reverb, a port of the Airwindows Galactic algorithm by Chris Johnson, verified against the original to the sample

params.text: Sets how much of the reverb's energy each incoming sample replaces: at 0 the tanks are frozen indefinitely, at 1 new audio takes them over quickly
Attenuates and inverts the replace CV
Sets the treble of the reverberated signal by moving the cutoff of an internal low-pass filter
Attenuates and inverts the brightness CV
Adds stereo phase distortion between the left and right outputs; low values sound purer and flatter, high values dissonant, and the middle gives a lush chorus
Attenuates and inverts the detune CV
Sets the size of the reverb tanks; changing it during a performance produces audible zipper noise
Attenuates and inverts the size CV
Balances the reverberated signal against the input: at 0 the output matches the input, at 1 it is entirely from the tanks
Attenuates and inverts the mix CV
Splits one polyphonic input cable into left and right, taking channel 1 as left and channel 2 as right, when only one audio input is patched
Sends both output channels to the left output as a 2-channel polyphonic signal, channel 1 left and channel 2 right, and the port labels change to a single 2
Empties the reverb tanks, fading the audio down and back up around the moment it clears

inputs.text: Left audio in; with the right input empty this one is halved and fed to both sides, and polyphonic channels are summed to one voltage
Right audio in; with the left input empty this one is halved and fed to both sides, and polyphonic channels are summed to one voltage
Varies how fast incoming audio replaces the contents of the reverb tanks
Varies the treble of the reverberated signal
Varies the stereo phase distortion between the output channels
Varies the size of the reverb tanks
Varies the balance between reverberated and dry audio
A gate or trigger that empties the reverb tanks; pressing the CLR button while a gate is patched inverts the sense of that gate

outputs.text: Left audio out, one channel unless polyphonic stereo output is switched on

menu: Toggle sensitivity on all attenuverters — divides the effect of every attenuverter on the panel by 10, or restores them all
Enable input stereo splitter — does what the button between the input ports does, taking channel 1 of a polyphonic cable in the left input as left and channel 2 as right
Send polyphonic stereo to L output — does what the button between the output ports does, sending both channels to the left output as one 2-channel signal
Low sensitivity — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: divides that knob's effect by 10 and marks the knob with an orange dot
Unipolar mode — on an attenuverter knob's own menu, not the panel menu: adds 5V to the CV on that control and clamps the result at zero
